newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end slightly lower, cars dominate.
newsitem.headline: German shares end slightly lower, cars dominate.

text.p: German carmakers formed the focus for share traders' attentions on Thursday, as Volkswagen AG advanced strongly in a market that otherwise ended lower, treading water after the hurly-burly of recent weeks.
Dealers had been expecting a brief period of retrenchment as the market tried to digest the movements of recent days.

"The market has seen a floor at 3,200 points, and a ceiling at around 3,450 points -- there's your range. The market is now happy to trade within that range for a while. Anything convincingly below 3,200 points, though, and the market is in trouble," a Frankfurt trader said.
The IBIS DAX index ended afternoon trade down 12.18 points, or 0.36 percent, at 3,352.58 points, while the June DAX DTB future was down 17 points at 3,362.5 points.

"Volkswagen is the major focus of the market, with investors jumping in and out all day. There are not enough volumes in the car stocks to lift the market, but there is enough to hold us up where we are," a broker in Frankfurt said.

Volkswagen breached the 1,000 mark threshold earlier in the day and went on to reach a high of 1,047.60 marks, before settling back to a record closing high of 1,046 marks by the end of the day, representing a rise of 93.95 points or 9.87 percent.

Other sectors were out of favour as investors watched the inexorable rise of Volkswagen. Dresdner Bank, which reported further details on its 1996 figures, was down 81 pfennigs, 1.38 percent, at 58 marks.
"The Dresdner Bank figures were just further details, but there is not much interest in the banks at the moment -- everyone just wants cars," said a trader.

BMW AG ended up 27 marks at 1,434 marks, a rise of 1.92 percent, just off an earlier all-time high of 1,440 marks. There was also strong interest in Daimler-Benz AG, which was up 2.75 marks, 2.14 percent, at 131.55 marks.
Other features included sportswear-maker Adidas AG, which was up 7.10 marks, 3.99 percent, at 185 marks after it reported a 43 percent increase in first-quarter 1997 sales to 1.7 billion marks.
